products.name: Zearn
products.note: Verified in the research for The AI Ready School. AI: Adaptive digital lessons. Use: K-5 math curriculum and digital lessons. Who: Teachers, students. Student age: Students through teacher or school accounts. Privacy: Signed state student data privacy agreement in the SDPC registry (Utah, 2020). Price: Free for one teacher and up to 35 students; $2,500 per school per year; PD $2,500 per school per year.

reading.body:
Zearn is a nonprofit selling adaptive K-5 math software at $2,500 per school per year, with a free tier capped at one teacher and 35 students.

The pricing structure is the most concrete fact here. A free tier that stops at 35 students is a trial sized to a single classroom, not a district. The paid tier is priced per school rather than per seat, which puts the cost decision in front of a principal or district budget holder rather than an individual teacher. Professional development is priced at the same $2,500 figure as the software itself, so a school adopting the program pays twice that number in year one.

The privacy detail is narrow but specific. A signed state student data privacy agreement exists in the SDPC registry for Utah, dated 2020. That covers one state and one agreement. It does not establish what the company does with student data elsewhere, and it does not describe the underlying technical safeguards.

Nothing in this data speaks to compute, buildings, or power. The product is described as adaptive digital lessons, which implies inference running somewhere, but the data gives no model, no hosting arrangement, and no infrastructure footprint. A reader looking for the compute layer behind education AI will not find it here. What the data does cover is the commercial shape of one nonprofit vendor: free at classroom scale, paid at school scale, with training sold alongside the software.

profile_text.body:
Zearn is a nonprofit whose site presents Zearn Math as a program built on the idea that learning with Zearn helps math make sense, with students exploring math through pictures, visual models, and real-life examples. The site's main public function is account access, offering a log in for existing users.

Its tracked product is Zearn, listed under education and research AI, described as adaptive digital lessons for a K-5 math curriculum. It is used by teachers and students, with student access through teacher or school accounts. Pricing is free for one teacher and up to 35 students, $2,500 per school per year, and $2,500 per school per year for professional development. A signed state student data privacy agreement is held in the SDPC registry, for Utah, 2020.
